clue.text: A little rash, yobbo gobbles string up to appear uninhibited

indicators.note: rash means hasty and reckless, so the words before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as part of the fodder

indicators.note: gobbles means swallows whole, so the yobbo word takes the next piece inside itself

parts.note: a yobbo is a lout, a loutish youth
to string up is to hang

explanation.surface: A slightly reckless thug wolfs down some string and then behaves without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like a skin complaint but signals the anagram, LETITAL; 'gobbles' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To let it all hang out is an idiom for behaving freely and without inhibition.

clue.text: Award asbo to granny punching good man still

indicators.note: punching means driving into, so the next pieces are thrust inside the saint's abbreviation

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a good man
a British offender under an ASBO (anti-social behaviour order) may be given an electronic tag
nan is a British word for a grandmother

explanation.surface: A delinquent pensioner gets an ASBO and is thumping a saintly fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO was a British court order against anti-social behaviour, often enforced by electronic tagging; 'punching' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water is still, not flowing, so the adjective is a synonym.

clue.text: See 21
Pump-action's isolated shot

indicators.note: shot in the sense of ruined or wrecked, so the letters of the next word are scrambled

explanation.surface: A pump-action gun's lone blast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pump-action' suggests a shotgun, but it is the heart's pumping; 'shot' rearranges ISOLATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Diastole is the phase of the heartbeat when the heart relaxes and refills, part of its pumping cycle.

clue.text: Muddy chants a little music

indicators.note: muddy means muddled or confused, so the letters of the next word are mixed up

explanation.surface: Indistinct singing offers a fragment of a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A snatch is a brief fragment, as of a song or tune.

clue.text: A pace into seawater, a departure from grass?

indicators.note: into places one piece inside the other, the pace going inside the seawater

parts.note: surf is breaking seawater
a trot is a running pace

explanation.surface: A horse trots into the sea, leaving the grassy fields behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Artificial turf is a substitute for real grass, so it departs from grass.

clue.text: Signs up?

parts.note: reads like enlisting, but means the band of star signs overhead in the sky

explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac is the belt of twelve astrological signs seen up in the heavens.

clue.text: Politician claims Leon the writer can clean up the holiday business

indicators.note: claims in the sense of takes possession of, so the politician holds the next pieces inside

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician
Leon Uris was the American novelist who wrote Exodus
a can is a tin
to dust is to clean up

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician says novelist Leon can tidy up the tourism trade.
explanation.walkthrough: Leon Uris wrote Exodus; 'claims' splits the politician's letters in two around the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The tourist industry is the commercial sector serving holidaymakers.

clue.text: Annexe's relieved state?

explanation.definitionFit: An extension is an annexe added to a building; whimsically, a former tension is relief.

clue.text: 15 button's capital, wanting its first letter second

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the capital loses its opening letter

parts.note: Oslo is the capital of Norway
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A tape machine's capital key, missing its first letter, comes second.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is VIDEOTAPE; 'second' looks like a position for the letter but gives MO.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow-motion button on a video player plays footage slowly.

clue.text: French artist paints only the back entrance

parts.note: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French painter

indicators.note: only the back means just the final letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A French painter only paints the rear view.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is the act or means of entering, an entrance.

clue.text: Raider unfortunately behind time — becoming more so?

indicators.note: behind means following, so the rearranged letters come after the time letter
unfortunately signals things gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A raider is regrettably late and getting later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' turns RAIDER into ARDIER; the definition plays on 'behind time', being late, becoming more so.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardier means later, more behind time than before.

clue.text: 'Orrible comic character demanding jelly

indicators.note: the dropped H of 'Orrible shows the initial H falling away

parts.note: Hagar the Horrible is a Viking in a newspaper comic strip

explanation.surface: A horrible cartoon figure insists on having jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: Hagar the Horrible is a comic strip Viking; written 'Orrible, the name is pronounced without its H, so HAGAR loses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a gelatinous substance from seaweed used as a jelly.

clue.text: Bridge game where players drop something — nothing this bad among lowered marks

definitions.text: Bridge game where players drop something

indicators.note: among places the next pieces inside the marks

parts.note: pocks are pitted marks sunk into a surface
O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: bad means faulty, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Card players drop something at bridge, with no marks so low as this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' gives HSTI; 'among' is the container signal. 'Bridge' suggests cards but is a real bridge over a stream, as in Winnie-the-Pooh.
explanation.definitionFit: Poohsticks, from Winnie-the-Pooh, involves dropping sticks off a bridge and watching which emerges first.

clue.text: Film tailless snake biting love during riotous date

indicators.note: biting means clamping teeth round, so the shortened snake encloses the rest
tailless means without its last letter

parts.note: a viper is a venomous snake

indicators.note: during places love inside the rearranged date
riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A snake without a tail bites, out of love, during a wild night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riotous' gives DETA, 'during' and 'biting' are container signals, and 'tailless' drops the last letter; 'Film' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To film something is to record it, as on videotape.

clue.text: Rex as it's written at the rear of mobile toilet

indicators.note: as here means held within, the king's letter placed inside the language

parts.note: rex is a Latin word, so the language in which it is written is Latin
R is short for rex, king

indicators.note: at the rear of means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A king's name as written on the back of a portable toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex is the Latin for king, abbreviated R as in ER; the end of 'mobile' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: A latrine is a basic toilet, especially in a camp or barracks.

clue.text: One's quick to slip in tongue, extracting tonsils finally

indicators.note: in places the slip inside the shortened language
extracting means pulling out, so a letter is removed from the language

parts.note: Farsi is the Persian tongue

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the next word

parts.note: to err is to slip up

explanation.surface: A tongue slip during a tonsillectomy, said quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's quick' reads as a person but is the car; 'extracting' and 'in' work on the language, Farsi.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ferrari is a famously fast Italian sports car.

clue.text: One left feeding short figure in operation

indicators.note: feeding means putting food into, so the next pieces go inside the shortened figure
short means missing its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: fifty is a figure, a number
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A lone figure on the left feeds a short person in surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' as ACE comes from cards; 'short' and 'feeding' work on the number, and 'figure' misleads toward a body shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A facelift is a cosmetic surgical operation to tighten facial skin.

clue.text: Failing to produce the intended result — a bit over, perhaps

definitions.text: Failing to produce the intended result

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be in some other order

explanation.surface: Missing the target, a little too far, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: Abortive describes an attempt that fails and comes to nothing.

clue.text: Ylper?

parts.note: a word meaning a reply written backwards, a response turned round

explanation.definitionFit: To answer back is to retort impertinently; here a reply written back to front.

clue.text: See 22
Collapse, with universal investment in US bank?

indicators.note: investment in means being put into, so the universal letter goes inside

parts.note: a buck is a US dollar, so a lender of dollars is a US bank
U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: A collapse caused by a worldwide investment in an American bank.
explanation.walkthrough: BUCK LENDER is a whimsical name for a bank lending dollars, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To buckle under is to give way or collapse under pressure.

clue.text: Heartless rabble's sensational shocker?

parts.note: heartless means unfeeling, cold
a shower is British slang for a useless rabble

explanation.surface: An unfeeling mob gives a shocking sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'what a shower' disparages a useless crowd; 'Heartless' looks like a remove-the-middle signal but is COLD.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold shower is a jolt to the senses, literally a shock to the skin.

clue.text: Divine, breaking window seal

indicators.note: breaking means straddling the gap, so the answer runs across the two words

explanation.surface: A divine spirit breaks the seal of a window.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine for water is to dowse with a rod.

clue.text: Knowing tune backwards, movement requiring no thought

indicators.note: backwards means the word for a tune is read right to left

parts.note: a song is a tune
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Knowing a tune backwards, a reflex movement needing no thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnostic means having spiritual knowledge, so knowing.

clue.text: Shakespearean king established Christmas should be rejected

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: set means fixed, established
Noel is Christmas

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean king rejects the established Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: SET + NOEL read backwards gives LEON TES.
explanation.definitionFit: Leontes is the jealous king of Sicilia in The Winter's Tale.

clue.text: Slurring, you drink to consume

indicators.note: slurring means running words together in speech, so the phrase is heard as one

parts.note: sup means drink, so you sup

explanation.surface: Slurring as you drink, you finish it off.
explanation.definitionFit: To use up is to consume entirely.

clue.text: Paramedic, say, has organ to keep safe, perhaps?

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so the organ holds the rearranged word

parts.note: the liver is a bodily organ

indicators.note: perhaps means maybe in another order, so letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A paramedic has an organ to keep safe, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' gives FESA; 'to keep' is the container signal, and 'Paramedic, say' is a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramedic is an example of someone who saves lives.
